title: throughput-credit-and-degradation-clauses-for-dedicated-capacity
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Draft contract language and operational definitions for Dedicated Capacity throughput guarantees, including a pragmatic error-budget model, measurement windows, credit calculation for under-provisioning, and interplay with autoscaling/fleet controls. The goal is a customer-facing clause set that is precise enough for billing and remediation, but flexible for engineering to implement without breaking our autoscaling safety limits.
acceptance_criteria: Contract snippet that legal can sign off on with explicit definitions for Committed Throughput, Measured Throughput, Burst Allowance, and Credit Formula
Error budget calculation documented and unit-tested in billing pipeline (reference ENG ticket)
Autoscaling interaction doc that prescribes behavior during partial SLA breaches (canary, throttling, fallback to lower-cost variants)
Example customer-facing dashboard mock illustrating measurement windows and credit balance
Signoff from Legal, Billing, and Runtime engineering on language and measurement approach

decisions: Measure Committed Throughput as requests-per-second (RPS) normalized to model weight; convert token-heavy payloads to equivalent RPS using model-specific coefficient.
Use a 30-day billing window for error budget calculation with 5-minute sampling buckets to compute sustained degradations.
Allow a configurable Burst Allowance for short spikes: 2x committed throughput for up to 10 minutes/day aggregated across the billing window without counting against error budget.
Credit formula: Credit = min(0.25 * monthly_commit_fee, monthly_commit_fee * (sum(underage_seconds * underage_ratio) / total_seconds_in_window)).
Autoscaler behavior during breach: prefer preemptive capacity top-up if available; otherwise throttle best-effort traffic and failover to lower-cost model variants before applying credits.
Customer must provide a 72-hour incident report window to be eligible for credits; immediate automatic credits only for clear measurement anomalies (instrumentation downtime).
proposed_contract_snippet: Definitions: 'Committed Throughput' means the aggregate requests-per-second (RPS) level committed by Customer in the Order Form for a given billing month, normalized per-model by Redwood's published model weights. 'Measured Throughput' means the 95th percentile of observed sustained RPS computed over 5-minute buckets across the billing window. 'Burst Allowance' means a short-duration allowance where Measured Throughput may exceed Committed Throughput up to 2x for a cumulative 10 minutes per billing month. Credit Mechanics: If Measured Throughput falls below Committed Throughput for sustained periods such that the aggregated under-provisioned-weighted-duration exceeds the Customer's Error Budget, Customer will be eligible for a service credit calculated as: Credit = min(MaxCreditCap, MonthlyCommitFee * (UnderageWeightedSeconds / TotalSecondsInWindow)). MaxCreditCap = 25% of MonthlyCommitFee. Notification & Remediation: Redwood will provide Customer with notice of an SLA breach within 5 business days of detecting underage and will commence an investigation. Customer may be eligible for credits upon completion of a mutually-agreed remediation and verification process. Exceptions: Instrumentation outages, force majeure, and customer misconfigurations documented in support tickets are excluded unless Redwood's telemetry shows clear evidence of a platform-side fault.
open_questions: Should we express Committed Throughput in tokens/sec for token-billed customers or normalize everything to RPS?
How should preemptible/spot capacity be treated in the measurement if customer commitment spans both guaranteed and burst pools?
What is the operational SLA for notifying customers (5 business days proposed) vs the legal notice period?
Do we want automatic credits for first-party incident durations shorter than 30 minutes to reduce ops friction?
